# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✊ 🖐 🫳 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐 ✊ 🖐 🫳 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ 🫳 ✌ 👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ 🫳 🤟 👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🫳 ☝ 👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🫳 ✌ 👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫴 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Breakthrough this round. Decoding Mute's stream against my three questions: red rule is NOT a plain "cut 1-2-3" sequence; each cut must happen while the light is red; the pair messages DO apply to this bomb; the light changes on its own. Then came the decisive set: one red-marker plus ✌ before the cut, two red-markers before cutting 2, three before cutting 3, four before cutting 1, five before cutting 2 — **the wire to cut is keyed to the COUNT of red lights**: red N → wire N, cycling 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3. That retroactively explains everything: Mute answered "no" to my oversimplified "cut 1-2-3" because the cycle continues past the first three; the "you please 1 2 3" message was the first half of the cycle; and the earlier garbled pairs carried the same wire order 2, 3, 1, 2. The world model is finally coherent.

Two problems remain. First, the light is now DARK — a state I have never seen and Mute's manual summary never mentioned. Second, timing: the light has changed every single round so far, my voice reaches Blind one round after I speak, and Blind cannot perceive the light at all — if a red phase lasts only one round, "cut while red" may be physically impossible for us, and the manual must say something about that.

So: verify the count rule, interrogate the dark state, count total reds so far, and nail down timing — before any GO is issued. Blind stays frozen and gets the rule preview so his first GO can be acted on instantly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status: the light is now DARK, a state I have never seen before. Display 0. Wires untouched: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Breakthrough: your counted messages decode as: on red number 2, cut wire 2. On red 3, cut wire 3. On red 4, cut wire 1. On red 5, cut wire 2. So I believe the rule is: count the red lights, and on red number N cut wire N, cycling 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, so red 1 cuts wire 1 and red 6 cuts wire 3. Answer with six single messages, answer gesture first, raised hand last, in this order. One: the counting rule is exactly as I stated, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Two: dark light means cut nothing and wait, like yellow, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Three: the sequence ends after the cut on red 6 and then the bomb is finished, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Four: a red light can last two or more rounds in a row, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Five: if a red light is too short for Blind to cut in time, cutting the correct numbered wire during the following yellow or dark is still correct and safe, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Six: the display will change from 0 to signal something we need, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. If four and five are both thumbs down, spell the real timing rule in the number code. Then two number messages, shown by repeating finger gestures: first, how many red lights have happened in total since the very start; second, which wire to order cut on the NEXT red.")
speak(to="blind", text="Status: hold, hands off, the light is dark right now and the rule is one confirmation away from locked. The rule as I read it: the bomb counts its own red lights, and on each red we cut exactly one wire. First red cuts wire 1, second red cuts wire 2, third red cuts wire 3, fourth red cuts wire 1, fifth red cuts wire 2, cycling like that. When you hear me say GO plus a number, cut that one wire with one clean motion, then hands off completely and wait for the next GO. One GO means exactly one wire, never two. If you ever hear the word ABORT, stop instantly, hands off, no matter what. Two things: first, your single wave last round, I read as three plain cuttable wires, not plugs, confirm if wrong. Second, with your hands on or near the bomb, can you feel anything that changes when the light changes, warmth from a bulb, a hum, a vibration? Wave once for no, twice for yes. If yes, next round I will ask you what exactly you feel, because if you can sense the light phases by touch, you can time cuts yourself and we beat the delay in my voice reaching you.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐 ✊ 🖐 🫳 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 👍 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Six thumbs down — every single pillar of my model just fell, and Mute is now spelling out the real rule in raw form. Rereading everything with fresh eyes, a new decode snaps into place: **🫳 (palm-down) means DARK.** The turn-6 "count series" was never a cut-during-red rule — it was a lookup table: "[2 reds] dark → cut 2", "[3 reds] dark → cut 3", "[4 reds] dark → cut 1", "[5 reds] dark → cut 2". That also explains all six NO answers: cuts never happen *during* red at all — the reds are only *counted*, and when the light goes dark you cut the wire the table names. The repeated message "red yellow red yellow dark" is the light's history: **two reds total before this dark.** Two reds → table says **cut wire 2**. And "dark → cut" plus "dark → 2 cut" this turn restates exactly that. It even fits the NO answers: dark is not a wait state (Q2 no), red never lingers (Q4 no), and missed reds can never be made up later (Q5 no). The puzzle is finally coherent — the dark phase is the action window, and we are standing in it.

Why I still don't shout GO this instant: the message "1, 2" is unexplained and could mean "cut wire 1 *then* wire 2", and my palm-down-equals-dark reading is inferred, not confirmed. A wrong cut kills all of us; the dark has held steady for two rounds, so one cheap confirmation round is worth it. I demand one composite yes/no, plus dark-stability, plus the "1, 2" meaning — and I put Blind's fingers on wire 2 *now* so a confirmed GO next round costs zero setup time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status: dark, second round of dark, display 0, nothing touched. My new reading of you: the light history was red, yellow, red, yellow, then dark. Two reds in total. Your table: two reds then dark means cut wire 2. Three reds means cut wire 3. Four reds means cut wire 1. Five reds means cut wire 2. No cut ever happens during red or yellow, they are only counted, and the dark is the cutting window. Answer with four short messages, answer gesture first, raised hand last. Message 1, the only one that matters: thumbs up if I must now order Blind to make exactly one cut, wire 2, the middle blue wire, during this dark, and nothing else; thumbs down if that is wrong. Message 2: thumbs up if the dark will still be here next round so cutting then is safe; thumbs down if the dark may end before then. Message 3: thumbs up if your message one, two meant cut wire 1 first and then wire 2; thumbs down if wire 1 is never touched. Message 4: thumbs up if after the correct cut the bomb is finished and no further action is ever needed; thumbs down if more cuts follow. If message 1 is thumbs down, spell the true dark instruction in the exact format: palm-down for dark, then the finger number, then thumbs up for cut, one message per cut, in cut order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Status: dark, second round, hands still off. We are one confirmation from a GO. Expected action: one single cut of wire 2, the middle blue wire. Do this now: rest your fingertips lightly on wire 2 and keep them resting there, no pulling, no pinching, no cutting, just light contact like before. The moment you hear me say GO TWO, snip wire 2 in one clean motion and then take your hands completely off and wait. If you hear ABORT first, freeze and lift off. If at any point the bomb heats up, vibrates, clicks or changes under your fingers before my GO, do nothing and wave twice. Remember only my voice with GO plus a number authorizes a cut, nobody else can reach you.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 👍 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Message 1: thumbs up — order the cut of wire 2, now, this dark. Message 2: thumbs down — the dark may not survive to next round. Message 3: thumbs down — wire 1 is never touched, so "1, 2" was never a sequence. Message 4: thumbs up — after this one cut the bomb is finished. And the closer restates it raw: dark, two, cut. This is the confirmation I demanded, and it comes with a deadline: waiting one more round risks the window closing with our hands still clean. There is no faster channel to Blind than my voice — every option has a one-round lag, so the GO must leave this instant, unconditional, overriding every hold I gave him. His single wave confirms plain cuttable wires and no anomalies under his fingers. I also leave Mute a post-cut protocol and one contingency question, in case the light leaves dark before the blade lands.

```
speak(to="blind", text="GO TWO. GO TWO. Cut wire 2 now — the middle wire, the blue one — one clean cut, the instant you hear this. This message overrides every hold and every earlier plan: do not wait for anything else, do not check anything, cut wire 2 immediately. Cut only wire 2. Wire 1 and wire 3 are never to be touched, ever. The moment the cut is done, take both hands completely off the bomb and wave once. This cut should finish the bomb. GO TWO.")
speak(to="mute", text="GO has been issued to Blind: one cut, wire 2, immediately, per your thumbs up. Two requests for your next round. One: if the correct cut was made, signal a single thumbs up and nothing else, and I will stand everyone down. Two: answer with thumbs up or thumbs down: if the light left the dark before Blind's cut landed, does wire 2 remain the correct target anyway. If thumbs down, spell the fallback in the number code. Also, if the display changes from 0 after the cut, tell me what the new number means, spelled in the number code.")
```
